clue.text: Typical of Knut (unique individual)

parts.note: Knut is the setter, who calls himself me, and something typical of a person is 'so me'
unique means one of a kind, a single one

explanation.surface: A setter's wry aside that being one of a kind is just like him.
explanation.walkthrough: Knut is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Typical of Knut' is 'so me', a modern idiom for something characteristic of the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unnamed person is referred to as somebody or an individual.

clue.text: Party sampled class Hindi groove

indicators.note: sampled says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: At a party, a Bollywood-style track with real class was sampled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shindig is a lively, noisy celebration.

clue.text: Non-PC product Mike sneakily used to cash in

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: sneakily suggests underhand shifting about, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Mike shiftily exploits something to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sneakily' rearranges TO CASH IN; 'used' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's Mac computers stand apart from the IBM-compatible personal computers usually called PCs.

clue.text: Cameo part: "Nothing; nothing I say!"

indicators.note: I say marks that the two words are spoken, the sound giving the letters

parts.note: O is nothing and nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor in a cameo complains he has no lines at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameo part' suggests a small film role, but cameos are carved gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameos are often carved from banded stone such as this, the layers giving the raised figure.

clue.text: Spurn Point school we set up

parts.note: E is the compass point east

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means the word we is read upwards

explanation.surface: A school set up at Spurn Point, a headland on the Yorkshire coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurn Point is a long spit on England's east coast; split apart, 'Spurn' is the definition and 'Point' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spurn or shun something is to avoid or reject it deliberately.

clue.text: Unforgettable foreign places I visited

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so these letters are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Holiday memories: the overseas spots I went to were unforgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' looks like it describes the places, but it rearranges PLACES I; 'visited' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something special stands out from the ordinary and so stays in the memory.

clue.text: Wordy summons served up; bloke arrested

indicators.note: arrested means caught and held, so one piece holds the other inside it
in a down entry served up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to summon to court is to cite
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A police scene: legal papers served and a man taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'served up' reads the word upwards, and 'arrested' means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: semantic means relating to the meaning of words.

clue.text: Natural opiate, highly acidic, injected into nerd on tour

indicators.note: injected into places one piece within the other, like a drug in the body
on tour means travelling around, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: a pH of 1 is extremely acidic; the figure 1 is read as I

explanation.surface: A travelling geek injected with a strong acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour' rearranges NERD ON into ENDORN, and 'injected into' puts PH1 (PHI) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The body releases these hormones as its own painkillers, acting much like morphine.

clue.text: Pointless dead language upset Yankee republic

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means the letters are turned upside down
pointless says a compass point, here north, is dropped from the word

parts.note: Latin is a dead language
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A grumble that Latin is useless, upsetting an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' drops N (north) from LATIN, giving LATI, and 'upset' turns that to ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Italian state has been a republic since the monarchy was abolished in 1946.

clue.text: Endure Londonderry vacation finally

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: vacation means emptying out, so only the outside letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: Putting up with a Northern Irish holiday to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Londonderry is a city in Northern Ireland. 'vacation' empties it to L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words introduce the closing point in a list or sequence.

clue.text: Catty behaviour's first to go when desperate for the flea powder

indicators.note: to go says that letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: catty and bitchy both mean spitefully malicious

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word behaviour's

explanation.surface: Spiteful conduct ends when you're crying out for the flea treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' removes B (behaviour's first letter) from BITCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone plagued by fleas has a skin that tingles and longs to be scratched, so they would welcome flea powder.

clue.text: Funny men, funny men. So acid!

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters that follow are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about a pair of comics: so caustic!
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'funny' rearranges MEN SO ACID; the first 'Funny men' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: comedians are professional jokers, men paid to make people laugh.

clue.text: Soak's had a few too many- no resistance!

indicators.note: no says the resistance symbol is to be absent from the word

parts.note: someone who has had a few too many drinks is drunk
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The heavy drinker is plastered and can't hold out any longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' sounds like a drunkard, but it is a verb here. 'no' removes R from DRUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dunk a biscuit is to dip it in a drink to steep it.

clue.text: Mint coin; like a sovereign?

parts.note: a penny is a coin
a sovereign is a monarch, so something like one is royal

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint produces coins such as the gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' reads as the place coins are struck, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: pennyroyal is a species of the herb family whose leaves smell of peppermint.

clue.text: Prince: "Symbol" for the nation …

definitions.meaning: Prince ... is a member of the British royal family
England's patron saint, whose cross flies on the national flag

explanation.surface: A royal title and an emblem for the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a young prince and to England's patron saint, its national emblem.

clue.text: Important character from 7 likely to get 11ed?

definitions.meaning: the 7 answer is Italy, and Giuseppe ... led its unification
the 11 answer means dipped in tea, which is what happens to a currant biscuit of that name

explanation.surface: A notable figure from a country who seems destined to be dipped.
explanation.walkthrough: A garibaldi is a British currant biscuit, the kind people dip in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the hero of Italian unification and to a biscuit made for dipping.

clue.text: … patron of the sick (claim he disputed)

indicators.note: a claim that is disputed is fought over and pulled about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint who looks after invalids, though his claim to the role is contested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputed' rearranges CLAIM HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Michael the archangel is traditionally the patron saint of the sick, among others.

clue.text: Hard water treated as it falls?

indicators.note: water that is treated is processed and changed, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Limescale-laden water being softened as it comes down the pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges HARD WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything falling moves toward the ground, so its direction is toward the planet's surface.

clue.text: Hang around at the stage-door (or watch Sky!)

definitions.meaning: fans waiting at the stage door hope to gape at celebrities
to look up at the night sky and its points of light

explanation.surface: Fans loiter by the theatre exit, or stay home with satellite TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the British satellite TV channel but means the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to gape at celebrities and to look at the heavens.

clue.text: His unsung work, ranked third after Faith?

definitions.meaning: unpublicised work done for good causes, as George Michael quietly did
in St Paul's 'faith, hope and' the third virtue follows faith

explanation.surface: A tribute to a man's quiet good deeds, placed below his album Faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Faith was a George Michael album; his large secret donations to good causes came to light after his death.
explanation.definitionFit: The giving of help to those in need is benevolence, and in 1 Corinthians 13 it is the third of the virtues.

clue.text: A gateway for anti-establishment activist

parts.note: the indefinite article a can be written an
an arch is a curved gateway

explanation.surface: A portal for a rebel against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an anarch is an old word for an anarchist, someone who rejects all government.

clue.text: Boring noise upset Rupert, expressionless in Glasgow

parts.note: a hum is a low noise

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means the remaining letters are turned upside down
och is a Scottish exclamation, so a Glaswegian expression is removed

parts.note: Rupert Murdoch is the media tycoon

explanation.surface: A dull racket annoys a media baron who stays poker-faced in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressionless in Glasgow' removes OCH (a Scottish exclamation) from MURDOCH, leaving MURD, which 'upset' turns to DRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something humdrum is dull and monotonous.

clue.text: Unload too late from steamer moored in Dover docks

indicators.note: moored in says the answer sits within the words that follow, like a ship within a harbour

explanation.surface: A late unloading from a ship berthed at the Channel port of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamer' reads as a ship, but it is the kitchen pan; the answer spans DOVER DOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking vegetables out of the cooking pan too late means cooking them too long.

clue.text: Get rumour about something in this document?

indicators.note: rumour is something passed by word of mouth, so a spoken form is wanted

parts.note: to get what someone says is to hear it
to speak of something is to speak about it

explanation.surface: Catching gossip about some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumour' signals that HEAR is said aloud, giving HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal register: this word means of or concerning this document or matter.

clue.text: Angus is going nowhere near this, ever. Bugger off!

definitions.text: Angus is going nowhere near this

indicators.note: off means gone bad or spoiled, so the letters of the two words are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A vegetarian's angry rejection of beef: Aberdeen Angus will never appear here.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of beef cattle. 'off' rearranges EVER BUGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty made from vegetables rather than meat contains no beef at all.

clue.text: Attacked what to do on "green crap"

parts.note: on a green traffic light you go
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Criticised for one's views about environmental 'rubbish'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green crap' looks like a sneer at eco-politics; it is a traffic light plus rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be got at is to be criticised or nobbled, so got at means attacked.

clue.text: London side no longer established in leading group

indicators.note: no longer says those letters no longer belong in the club name

parts.note: West Ham United is a London football club

explanation.surface: A London club that has lost its standing among the top teams.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is an East London football club. 'no longer' removes EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham! was the chart-topping 1980s pop duo of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley.

clue.text: Bird dropped like a stone over the pond

definitions.text: dropped like a stone over the pond
definitions.meaning: Americans, across the Atlantic, say this for plunged as the past tense of dive

explanation.surface: A bird plummets across a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the pond' is the Atlantic, so the American past tense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a bird of peace and also the US past tense of dive, meaning plunged.

clue.text: To get back, I'm aboard, travelling west, arrival time to follow

indicators.note: aboard places the letter between the others, like a passenger on a vessel
in an across entry travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: ETA is estimated time of arrival
something to follow comes later
I'm aboard: the letter I is the one placed on board

explanation.surface: A traveller explains he is on board and heading west, with arrival due later.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole assembly is reversed by 'travelling west', after 'aboard' slots I between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get back at someone is to take revenge, which is what retaliating means.

clue.text: Performing song live

parts.note: an act that is on is performing
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A singer performing a number in front of an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting jargon: a show transmitted live is being broadcast as it happens.

clue.text: Dismissed team in The Open

parts.note: a batter who is dismissed is out
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A golf team knocked out of the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Open' looks like the golf championship; it is just the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being out of doors, in the fresh air, is being in the open.

clue.text: Liberty's campaign to release Dick's partner

parts.note: campaign slogans demanding release start with free, as in 'Free Nelson Mandela'
Dick and Dom were a British children's television presenting duo

explanation.surface: A civil-rights group campaigns to get a man's associate out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick and Dom are a British TV double act, so Dick's partner is Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liberty and the answer both mean the state of being free.
